hypotheses.reasoning: notification-svc's heap kept growing after each full GC and the old gen was never reclaimed: 78% at 22:31:59, 84% at 22:34:35 and 90% at 22:38:35, with GC overhead climbing from 20% to 50%. It then hit OutOfMemoryError in messageCache.put and was OOMKilled at the 2Gi limit three times (restart counts 1 to 3). The gateway's 502s ('connection reset / no healthy upstream') start right after the first OOM kill at 22:38:53 and come in bursts that line up with the crash-restart cycles. That pattern points to a memory leak or unbounded messageCache. I found no deploy or config change in the window. Red herrings: one malformed message was cleanly moved to the DLQ (#30), and a slow audit_log query in notif-db (#73) is unrelated.
A recent change to messageCache could have caused the leak, but no deploy or version event shows up in these logs.
One message failed schema validation in notif-worker but was dead-lettered right away. It doesn't explain the OOMs in notification-svc.

verdict.recommendedAction: Restore capacity now: raise the notification-svc memory limit or add replicas, and stagger restarts so at least one healthy pod stays up. Take a heap dump before the next OOM. Fix the leak by putting a size limit plus TTL/LRU eviction on messageCache. Add alerts on old-gen heap after GC.
